q: What is the climate like in Bihać, Bosnia?
a: Bihać has a moderate continental climate with warm summers and cold, damp winters. The town lies at about 230 metres above sea level and gets an average of around 1,300 mm of rain and snow a year. Rainfall is spread throughout the year, so there is no really dry season. Summers are pleasant for swimming in the Una, while winters bring snow and frost.

q: How hot does Bihać get in summer?
a: In July and August the average daytime highs in Bihać are around 26 to 27 °C, while nights are cooler, at about 13 °C. During heatwaves temperatures can exceed 35 °C. It feels noticeably cooler by the Una than in the town centre.

q: How cold is Bihać in winter?
a: In January the average daytime high in Bihać is around 4 °C and the night-time low around -4 °C. Colder days with hard frost are not unusual, especially when a cold north wind blows. Winters are damp, so it often feels colder than the thermometer suggests.

q: What is the warmest month in Bihać?
a: The warmest month in Bihać is July, with an average daily temperature of around 20 °C and highs of about 27 °C. August is almost as warm. This is also the best time for swimming in the Una. By the river and in the shade it feels noticeably cooler in summer than out in the open.

q: What is the coldest month in Bihać?
a: The coldest month in Bihać is January, with an average daily temperature of around 0 °C. At night the temperature regularly drops below freezing, and snow is possible from December to March. December and February are only slightly milder. In winter, bring warm clothes and shoes with good grip.

q: What is the weather like in Bihać in spring?
a: In March daytime temperatures in Bihać are around 11 °C, in April around 16 °C and in May around 21 °C. Spring is rainy, and this is when the Una is at its highest and the waterfalls are most powerful. April nights are still cold, so bring warmer clothes.

q: What is the weather like in Bihać in autumn?
a: In September daytime temperatures in Bihać are still around 22 °C, in October around 17 °C and in November around 11 °C. September is often settled and pleasant for day trips, while November is the wettest month of the year. Autumn mornings by the river are often misty.

q: When is the rainy season in Bihać?
a: Bihać gets the most rain in November, on average around 140 to 160 mm. Rain is also frequent in spring, especially in April and May. July is the driest month, but summer showers and thunderstorms are not unusual. For trips in spring and late autumn, bring an umbrella and a waterproof jacket.

q: Does it snow in Bihać?
a: Yes, it snows in Bihać every winter, mostly from December to February and sometimes in March. According to the long-term average, there is snow on the ground for around ten to fifteen days a month in January and December, but in recent years winters have often been milder. On nearby Plješevica and Grmeč the snow lasts longer.

q: What is the best time of year to visit Bihać?
a: For most visitors, June and September are best, when it is warm but without the peak summer crowds. July and August are ideal for swimming in the Una and rafting at lower water levels. For powerful waterfalls and lush greenery come in May, and for autumn colours in October.

q: When is the best time for rafting on the Una river?
a: Rafting on the Una usually runs from spring to autumn, and July and August are the most comfortable for families and beginners, as the water is lower and it is warmer. In May and June the water level is higher, so rafting is more lively. We organise rafting with Una Olympic Rafting from Grmuša, so send us your date on +387 61 591 320.

q: Can you go rafting on the Una in April?
a: Rafting is possible in April, but the water is cold and the level is often high, so everything depends on conditions on the river. Operators provide wetsuits at this time and choose the section according to the water level. For exact information on your date, ask us; we arrange rafting with Una Olympic Rafting.

q: When is the best time to photograph the Una river?
a: For powerful waterfalls and lush greenery, May and June are best, while the water level is still high. In summer the water has its most striking turquoise and green colour, especially on a sunny day. In October the woods along the canyon turn yellow and red, which makes for quite different photos.

q: When are the autumn colours best around Bihać?
a: The autumn colours in the woods around the Una are usually at their best from mid to late October, depending on that year's weather. There are fewer tourists then, and the days are still often sunny. Bring warmer clothes for the mornings, which are cold and misty by the river.

q: Is October a good time to visit Bihać and Plitvice?
a: Yes, October is excellent for trips to Bihać and Plitvice, as the woods are in their autumn colours and there are fewer crowds than in summer. Daytime temperatures are around 15 to 17 °C, with colder nights. Plitvice is about 35 km from Bihać, a 35 to 40-minute drive via the Izačić border crossing.

q: What is Bihać like in winter?
a: In winter Bihać is a quiet town with fewer tourists and lower accommodation prices. The Una looks especially beautiful in the snow, and the waterfalls can partly freeze in hard frost. For a winter stay, choose a property with good heating, which you can ask about in your enquiry on apartmanibihac.com.

q: Is there skiing near Bihać?
a: Bihać has no ski resort of its own, but the surrounding area is mountainous, with Plješevica and Grmeč, where there is snow in winter. For proper ski resorts with lifts, people usually go further, to other parts of Bosnia or Croatia. Before setting off, check whether your chosen resort is open and what the road conditions are.

q: Is Una National Park open in winter?
a: Some parts of Una National Park can be visited in winter, but opening hours and access to some entrances depend on the season and road conditions. Snow can make it harder to reach the higher parts of the park. Before a winter visit, check the information on the park's official website, npuna.com.

q: When is the water level of the Una highest?
a: The Una is usually at its highest in spring, from March to May, when snow melts and rain is heavy, and it is often high in late autumn after the November rains as well. That is when waterfalls such as Štrbački buk are most powerful. In summer the water level is lowest and the water clearest.

q: Does the Una river dry up in summer?
a: The Una does not dry up even in summer, as it is fed by karst springs, but the water level is noticeably lower than in spring. The waterfalls are still beautiful, and the river becomes calmer and clearer. This is the best time for swimming and family rafting. For powerful waterfalls, though, spring is better.

q: How cold is the water in the Una in summer?
a: The Una is a cold river even in summer, as it is fed by springs, so the water is usually much colder than the sea. At calmer, shallower spots further downstream the water warms up more on hot days. Swimming is refreshing, but do not stay in the cold water too long.

q: When can you swim in the Una river?
a: July and August are best for swimming in the Una, and in warm years also late June and early September. Air temperatures are then around 25 to 30 °C and the water level is lower. Swim at calm spots and avoid areas near waterfalls and rapids.

q: Is August a good time for a holiday in Bihać?
a: Yes, August is one of the warmest and most popular months in Bihać, with temperatures of around 26 °C and higher. It is the time for swimming in the Una, rafting and summer events in town. Book accommodation for August early and send your enquiry on apartmanibihac.com.

q: Is the summer heat in Bihać bearable?
a: Generally yes, as nights in Bihać are cooler than on the coast, and shade and the nearby Una offer relief. During heatwaves, however, daytime temperatures can exceed 35 °C. On hot days the riverside houses in Lohovo, Pritoka and Grmuša are especially pleasant.

q: Is it often foggy in Bihać?
a: Yes, fog is common in Bihać in autumn and winter, especially in the mornings by the river. It usually lifts by midday but can slow down driving and traffic on the way to the border. Morning mist over the Una makes for special photos. If you drive towards Plitvice early in the morning, allow for slower progress.

q: What is the weather like in Bihać in May?
a: In May daytime temperatures in Bihać are around 20 to 21 °C, with nights around 9 °C. May is green and fairly rainy, and the Una has a high water level and powerful waterfalls. It is a good month for walks and photography, but still too cold for swimming.

q: What is the weather like in Bihać in June?
a: In June daytime temperatures in Bihać are around 24 °C, with nights around 12 °C. Nature is in full leaf and the Una's water level gradually drops. By late June it is often warm enough for a first swim and rafting. June is a good month for walks along the Una and trips to Plitvice before the busiest period.

q: What is the weather like in Bihać in September?
a: In September daytime temperatures in Bihać are around 22 °C, with nights around 10 °C. The weather is often settled and sunny, and there are fewer crowds than in August. In warmer years the first half of September is still suitable for swimming in the Una.

q: What is the weather like in Bihać in March?
a: In March daytime temperatures in Bihać are around 11 °C, with nights around freezing. Snow is still possible, especially early in the month, and the Una swells with snowmelt. Bring a warm jacket, waterproof shoes and an umbrella. March is a quiet month, with few tourists and lower accommodation prices.

q: What is the weather like in Bihać in December?
a: In December daytime temperatures in Bihać are around 5 °C, with nights below freezing. December is damp, with rain and snow, and the days are short. For a holiday-season stay, choose accommodation with good heating, which the owner confirms in the reply to your enquiry.

q: What should I pack for a summer trip to Bihać?
a: For summer, bring light clothing, swimwear, water shoes and sun protection. A thin jacket is useful for evenings by the river, which can be cool. For trips to the waterfalls and hiking you need comfortable trainers or walking shoes.

q: What should I pack for a winter trip to Bihać?
a: For winter in Bihać, bring a warm jacket, hat, gloves and waterproof shoes with good grip. If you are coming by car, winter tyres are essential, and there may be snow at border crossings and on mountain roads. Pack layers too, as it can be warm indoors.

q: What should I pack for Bihać in spring or autumn?
a: For spring and autumn, it is best to pack layers: T-shirts, a jumper, a waterproof jacket and an umbrella. Mornings and evenings are cold, while days can be warm. For walks along the Una, bring footwear that can handle mud and wet paths. Forest ground can be muddy even after a few dry days.

q: Do I need winter tyres to drive in Bosnia?
a: Yes, in Bosnia and Herzegovina winter equipment is compulsory from 1 November to 1 April, regardless of the weather. That means winter tyres on all wheels or, with summer tyres that have at least 4 mm of tread, snow chains ready in the car. If you come via Plitvice, in Croatia the period from 15 November to 15 April applies on roads designated for winter conditions.

q: Is Bihać worth visiting all year round?
a: Yes, Bihać has something to offer all year: swimming and rafting in summer, powerful waterfalls in spring, autumn colours in the woods and peace and snow in winter. It is busiest in July and August. Accommodation on apartmanibihac.com is available all year, and the price depends on the season.

q: When is Bihać least busy with tourists?
a: Bihać has the fewest tourists from November to March, when there is no rafting or swimming. Accommodation and services are quieter then, and prices are lower. If you do not mind the cold, it is a good time for a peaceful break and walks along the Una. Spots such as Štrbački buk are also quieter then.

q: When is the main tourist season in Bihać?
a: The main season in Bihać runs from June to September, peaking in July and August. This is when there are the most visitors, rafting trips and events on the Una. For that period, book accommodation a few weeks ahead, by enquiry on apartmanibihac.com or via WhatsApp on +387 61 591 320.

q: Are there severe summer storms in Bihać?
a: In summer, short and heavy showers with thunder are possible in Bihać, usually in the afternoon after a hot day. They tend to pass quickly, but stay off the river and away from exposed high ground while they last. Check the forecast before rafting or hiking. Rafting is postponed or stopped when there is thunder.

q: Where can I check the weather forecast for Bihać?
a: You can check the forecast for Bihać on the website of the Federal Hydrometeorological Institute of Bosnia and Herzegovina and in the usual weather apps. For the Una's water level, it is worth asking rafting operators, as they monitor the river daily. We are also happy to tell you what the weather is like before your arrival.

q: Is spring a good time to see the Una waterfalls?
a: Yes, spring is the best time for the waterfalls, as the water level is at its highest and Štrbački buk and Martin Brod are at their most powerful. Paths can be wet and slippery, so bring good footwear. The entrance to Una National Park near Bihać is about 15 minutes' drive from town.
